claims.claim: The faintest supernova observed remained visible for nearly a year and appears linked to a white dwarf with a small companion star.
claims.episode_span: The faintest supernova on record stayed visible nearly a year.
claims.source_title: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
claims.supporting_quote: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star.

claims.claim: A proposed nuclear thermal mission to Ceres would cut the trip time to roughly one year and allow water extraction for propellant.
claims.episode_span: Nuclear thermal rockets operate at two to three times the efficiency of chemical rockets, cutting the Earth-to-Ceres trip to roughly one year.
claims.source_title: Nuclear Pathfinder Mission To Ceres Would Usher In Era Of Interplanetary Transport
claims.supporting_quote: Nuclear thermal rockets operate at two to three times the efficiency of chemical rockets and can make the trip from Earth in a little over a year, says Worden.

claims.claim: The UK Space Agency released its Technical Framework on Lunar Operations on 23 November 2026.
claims.episode_span: The UK Space Agency released its Technical Framework on Lunar Operations on 23 November 2026, establishing standards for trajectory deconfliction, planetary protection, spectrum allocation, and space nuclear systems.
claims.source_title: UK Space Agency Lunar Operations Framework 2026
claims.supporting_quote: On 23 and 26 November 2026, the UK Space Agency issued two landmark governance documents—the Technical Framework on Lunar Operations and updated Unlocking Space for Government guidance

claims.claim: Magellan radar data show a dark spot 20 km wide inside bright halos spanning 180 km on Venus with no central crater visible.
claims.episode_span: A radar image from NASA’s Magellan spacecraft shows a dark spot roughly 20 kilometers wide inside two bright halos on Venus, the fainter outer halo spanning 180 kilometers.
claims.source_title: Meteor blast scars hint at Venus's gradual volcanic makeover
claims.supporting_quote: In a radar image from NASA's Magellan spacecraft, a dark spot about 20 kilometers (12 miles) wide sits inside two bright halos on Venus (see images C and D above). The fainter outer halo spans some 180 kilometers (110 miles), yet there is no obvious crater at the center.
